content:
anya: quick heads-up — I'm bringing stratus-6.5p into the onboarding pipeline for evals + int8 experiments. weights are from upstream release.

mike: do we have the license text attached? any commercial restrictions we should know about?

anya: added link to the repo and pasted the license in the PR description. it's not a simple MIT/Apache header.

liz: glanced briefly — upstream used a custom "Non-Commercial Hosting" clause. will paste the exact bit here.

liz: ```\nSection 3.c: 'Model may be used for research and internal purposes. Public hosting or commercial serving of model-derived inference is prohibited without explicit commercial license.'\n```

sam: hmm. so running evaluation and internal quantization is fine, but exposing an API (hosted) or offering it on Redwood Dedicated could be a violation.

mike: what about Private deployments (VPC/on-prem)? customers run in their infra — does that count as "hosting" by upstream?

liz: typically private customer-managed deployments are allowed if no redistribution of weights occurs. the clause is ambiguous — "public hosting" seems the blocker. need clarification from upstream to be safe.

anya: do we need to block adding it to hosted model catalog then? I can add a catalog flag if legal wants that.

liz: yes please block in hosted and dedicated by default. mark as "require-commercial-license" and "clarify-hosting-rights". I'll open a clarification ticket with upstream.

license-bot: Created ticket LEG-1085 and assigned to liz. (https://redwood.atlassian.com/LEG-1085)

sam: another question: is quantizing to int8 considered a derivative that would trigger attribution or redistribution clauses? the license mentions "derivative works" but not formats.

liz: quantization/optimization is generally a transformation; it's allowed for internal use. redistribution (weights or model binaries) is restricted. include the original license and attribution in metadata if we surface this model anywhere.

mike: ok I'll add a note to the onboarding checklist: "do not enable hosted/dedicated until commercial rights cleared; private deployments allowed with attribution metadata." and add catalog tag `restricted-hosting`.

anya: meantime I'll run evals locally and post perf/regression numbers here. if upstream replies with a commercial license, we can re-evaluate.

sam: running baseline bench + rouge/f1/latency tests now; will share a short summary in ~45m.

liz: thanks — I'll follow up with upstream and update LEG-1085. if they refuse commercial hosting, we may still onboard to private-only channels with clear metadata and a notice.

anya: perfect. marking this thread as in-progress. :white_check_mark:
